newsitem.title: UK: CATS group wins UK gas case against Enron.
newsitem.headline: CATS group wins UK gas case against Enron.

text.p: The CATS (Central Area Transmission System) parties succeeded in their case against Teesside Gas Transportation Limited (TGTL), a subsidiary of Enron Corp in the High Court in London on Tuesday.
The court found that TGTL was not entitled to terminate the capacity reservation and transportation agreement in April 1996. The judgement added that TGTL's counter claim had failed.

The judge found in a written ruling that the CATS parties are entitled to a declaration that since April 1 1993 TGTL has been liable to pay for capacity under the CRTA (Capacity Reservation and Transportation Agreement).

CATS is owned by Amoco with a 29.5 percent stake, Amerada Hess (17.7 percent), British Gas Exploration and Production Ltd (39.4 percent), Phillips Petroleum Co (UK) Ltd , Fina Exploration Ltd (0.57 percent) and Agip(UK)Ltd (0.34 percent).
The judgement also found that payment and interest should be made for the time since TGTL stopped paying. It also dismissed TGTL's counter claim.
The case arose out of a contract between TGTL and the CATS parties for transport of gas from the North Sea J-Block through CATS. TGTL booked capacity under the CRTA in 1990 to run from April 1993.
But TGTL stopped paying in October 1994 and the CATS parties filed a writ to recover payment in March 1995.
Enron then counter claimed saying that the transport facilities were not as specified in the contract, but the High Court dismissed this claim.
On Monday Enron as purchaser of gas from J-BLock settled a dispute with the block's producers, Phillips Petroleum, BG Exploration and Production Limited, and Agip UK Ltd.
